sections.h2: The Rule of 72 is within a tenth of a year for rates of 6% to 10%

chart.title: Between 6% and 10%, the rule misses doubling time by a tenth of a year or less
chart.sub: Rule-of-72 estimate minus exact doubling time, years.
chart.source: Exact figures from n = ln(2) / ln(1 + r).

sections.means: The rule overstates doubling time at low rates and understates it above about 8%, so it is a rough check rather than an exact figure.
sections.todo: Use the exact formula n = ln(2) / ln(1 + r) whenever a projection will be relied on.

sections.h2: The same rates give tripling in 16.1 years and quadrupling in 20.3 at 7.1%

chart.title: At 7.1%, a deposit doubles in 10.1 years, triples in 16.1 and quadruples in 20.3
chart.sub: Years to reach each multiple at a 7.1% annual rate, using the rounded constants 72, 114 and 144.
chart.source: Ministry of Finance small-savings notification, Q2 FY2026-27.

sections.means: Quadrupling is simply doubling twice, so the 144 rule is exactly twice the 72 rule at every rate.
sections.todo: Read the 114 and 144 columns as rough guides, since both constants are rounded up from their exact values.

sections.h2: After inflation, the PPF's real return of about 2.1% takes 34 years to double

chart.title: After roughly 5% inflation, the same PPF deposit takes about 34 years to double
chart.sub: Years to double, nominal rate against real rate after inflation.
chart.source: Figures as stated in the article.

sections.means: Once inflation is subtracted, the PPF's growth in purchasing power is far slower than the headline rate suggests.
